To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
social isolation in mice is associated with an enhanced neurotoxic action of ethanol, which is likely to be mediated by increased local release of 3α, 5α-tetrahydroprogesterone in the hippocampus.

social isolation in C57BL6 mice is associated with reduced levels of excitability and LTP in hippocampal CA1 pyramdial neurons, which are further inhibited by exposure to 40 mM ethanol, and that this effect of ethanol is abolished by co-administration of 1 μM finasteride.

social isolation (i) decreases neuronal excitability in CA1 pyramical neurons of C57BL/ 6J mice; (ii) decreases the extent of L-TP in CA1 pyrimal neurons; and (iii) increases sensitivity to ethanol-induced inhibition of LTP in these neurons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of neurosteroids in the effects of ethanol on hippocampal synaptic plasticity and behavior.

the effects of social isolation (SI), an animal model of stress and anxiety, on the neurosteroid-mediated inhibitory effects of ethanol (EtOH) on hippocampal synaptic plasticity and neuronal excitability.
the role of neurosteroids in the regulation of hippocampal plasticity and behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

social isolation in mice results in a decrease in neuronal activity and synaptic plasticity that is likely associated with the increased sensitivity of the hippocampus to the inhibitory effects of EtOH.
SI mice have a decreased neuronal excitability and reduced LTP.

the increased sensitivity of the CA1 region to the neurosteroidal effect of EtOH induced by SI likely underlies the increased sensitivity to EtOH-induced inhibition of LTP in SI compared to group-housed C57BL/7J mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the increased sensitivity of the hippocampus to the neurosteroidal effect of EtOH in socially isolated mice may contribute to the increased sensitivity to EtOH-induced impairment of learning and memory in these animals.
SI mice have decreased neuronal excitability, decreased synaptic plasticity, and increased sensitivity to the inhibitory effect on LTP of EtOH.
the neurosteroidogenesis induced by chronic exposure to EtOH in the hippocampus of SI animals is enhanced, resulting in an enhanced inhibition of LTP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of social isolation on the brain is not limited to the hypothalamus and the amygdala.

social isolation in C57BL6 mice leads to reduced neuronal excitability and plasticity, which is consistent with the reduced LTP and the increased sensitivity to EtOH-induced inhibition of LTP in slices prepared from SI animals.
social isolation (i.e., a form of stress) results in reduced levels and/or function of neuronal excitability in the hippocampus of C57BL/ 6J mice.
